root_cause.text: The driver conditionally freed the RSS context's VNIC in firmware only when the network interface was running (`netif_running()`), leading to a firmware VNIC resource leak when RSS contexts are deleted while the interface is down, causing resource exhaustion and potential failure to restore RSS contexts on interface up.
root_cause.evidence: The patch removes the `if (netif_running(bp->dev))` guard from `bnxt_del_one_rss_ctx()` so that `bnxt_hwrm_vnic_free_one()` and related VNIC context free calls are always executed, regardless of interface state. The commit message explicitly states: "Having that condition will make the driver leak VNICs in FW whenever close() happens with active RSS contexts."

The commit message explicitly states: "Having that condition will make the driver leak VNICs in FW whenever close() happens with active RSS contexts."

candidates.rationale: This condition guards the firmware VNIC free operations, causing them to be skipped when the interface is down, leading to resource leak.
This firmware call to free the VNIC is only executed when netif_running() is true, so it is skipped when the interface is down, leaking the resource.
This loop is part of the conditional block that only runs when the interface is running, so the VNIC context freeing inside the loop is skipped when the interface is down.
This inner condition and the subsequent free are only executed when the outer if is true, contributing to the resource leak when the interface is down.
This firmware call to free VNIC context is skipped when the interface is not running, causing a firmware-side resource leak.

vuln_statements.explanation: This conditional guard causes the entire VNIC freeing block to be skipped when the network interface is not running, leading to a firmware VNIC resource leak when RSS contexts are deleted with the interface down.

This firmware call to free the VNIC is only executed when netif_running() is true; when the interface is down, it is skipped, causing the VNIC to remain allocated in firmware and leaking the resource.

This loop is part of the conditional block that only runs when the interface is running. When skipped, the per-context free operations inside are not performed, contributing to the firmware resource leak.
This inner condition is only evaluated when the outer if (netif_running) is true. When the interface is down, the check never happens, and valid RSS context IDs remain allocated in firmware.
This firmware call to free a VNIC context is skipped when the interface is not running, directly causing the firmware-side resource leak for each RSS context ring.
